newsitem.title: UK: LME marking time at week's end, prices close mixed.
newsitem.headline: LME marking time at week's end, prices close mixed.

text.p: Base metal markets were slightly uncertain during late Friday LME trading, with the complex's leading lights marking time after some healthy gains earlier this week, traders said.

Nevertheless, the midsesission dip that halted the initial run-up was not sustained, and by the close there were signs that the investment funds who are the driving force behind the current rally were back in the frame.
"We saw a quiet morning, but it was looking stronger towards the close," William Adams of LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co said.
Zinc touched a fresh 4-1/2 year high at one stage today, but largely spent the session consolidating the gains notched up in mid-week, with funds less active.
Last business was at $1,332 a tonne, up just $2 from Thursday's kerb. The upside objective remains around $1,350.
Copper prices again encountered difficulty at the $2,400 level - the market's current "bete noire" - against a background of a slight softening in the spread.
The minimal 425-tonne rise in stocks did not have any significant impact on the market, which closed at $2,390, up just $2. The cash/threes backwardation was at $55/60.
Aluminium also suffered at overhead resistance pegged just above $1,670, which prevented the market capitalising on a 4,225-tonne fall in stocks - the latest in a long run of inventory drawdowns.

Despite some trader scepticism over the stock falls, which may not all lreflect actual offtake but represent consignment business instead, aluminium still seems set to push towards $1,700. Last kerb trade was at $1,662, an $8 loss.
Nickel maintained its uptrend, and rose above stubborn selling around $7,800 to finish at $7,830, up $60.
However, other metals sagged, with lead shedding $14 at $622 and tin losing $30 to conclude at $5,880. Alloy was indicated at a slightly softer $1,500/07 a tonne.
